rites.name: Vontor
rites.text: A fighting technique of ancient origin in which the practitioner jabs a foe with a rigid, open hand held like a spear point. It is known as a favored strike of one skilled fighter.

rites.name: Syisith
rites.text: Syisith is the concept of the first sounding of Osuvaeno, the note that drew the roots of the world together in the Singing. In the Age of the first sovereign it is remembered as the pull that gave the groves their shape and let the first kingdoms grow.

rites.name: Seraulia
rites.text: A basic battle posture where the fighter lowers a shoulder and charges straight at an enemy. The shoulder guards the body during the rush, and the fighter can chain further strikes while still moving forward.

rites.name: Amauntes
rites.text: A fighter wraps both legs around an opponent's neck, then twists sharply to break it and leave the foe senseless. The move is quick and decisive.

rites.name: Oreonentes
rites.text: A grappling method in which the practitioner wraps an arm around an attacker's arm and drives a forceful blow into the opponent's midsection to halt an incoming assault.

rites.name: Ameostines
rites.text: A straight strike that carries a surge of inner energy. The fighter crosses both hands, lifts the front leg, then steps quickly forward and drives the punch into the opponent.

rites.name: Ameonellus
rites.text: A defensive maneuver where a fighter turns the arms in a spinning motion to blunt and weaken an incoming strike. It belongs to a disciplined martial art of body movement.

rites.name: Maunanum
rites.text: A fighting discipline made of many numbered forms, each aimed at an opponent's most fragile body spots. Practitioners strike the stomach and knee, then throw, or unleash a rapid barrage ending in a low kick, or counter a punch and answer quickly.

rites.name: Corallium
rites.text: A grappling hold where a fighter crosses both arms over an opponent's throat, pressing the neck in a choking manner. It is used to subdue foes in close combat.

rites.name: Amasestium
rites.text: A fighter lifts one leg high over the head and then brings it down with great force onto an opponent's crown. It is a heavy strike aimed straight from above.

rites.name: Amarnia
rites.text: A grappling method in which a fighter seizes an opponent's head from behind and spins both bodies together, snapping the neck in the same motion.

rites.name: Oreoria
rites.text: A close-quarters striking method in which the fighter drives an elbow sharply into the flank of an opponent's torso. It is a quick, compact blow meant to end an exchange at short range.

rites.name: Lelum
rites.text: A fighter drives a tightly clenched palm into an opponent's shoulder with great force. It is a strike used to break an enemy's guard in close combat.

rites.name: Tastellor
rites.text: A fighter leaps down onto a foe and crashes the full weight of the body directly on top of them. It is a crushing grappling maneuver.

rites.name: Coristornum
rites.text: A combat discipline built on answering an attack at the moment it lands, turning the adversary's own momentum back against them. It is practiced by a single fighter known for mastering it.

rites.name: Coria
rites.text: A trainee grips a tall wooden post with arms, legs, or both, sliding up or down it to evade an opponent. Skilled practitioners of this discipline demonstrate fluid mastery of the movement.

rites.name: Serenosium
rites.text: A fighter whirls the body in a violent spin, pushing away every foe within reach. It is a reply made the instant an attack arrives.

rites.name: Valontium
rites.text: A movement art in which a practitioner accelerates so swiftly that onlookers perceive them as having vanished from sight.

rites.name: Lianaulum
rites.text: A ground-based strike where the fighter drives a forward kick toward the opponent's body, launched from a low position on the floor.

rites.name: Serintes
rites.text: A fighter's open hand is spun into a rotating edge that drives through a target with piercing force. Practitioners follow a deflecting turn with this strike to gouge deep wounds.

rites.name: Nerniastor
rites.text: A close-quarters fighting technique in which the user drives a rapid volley of flat-handed strikes into an adversary at short range.

rites.name: Masternum
rites.text: Fighters draw on seething wrath to push past their own bounds, striking fiercely and seldom holding back. Their strength grows instinctive, and some lose themselves to beastlike rage.

rites.name: Siasauntum
rites.text: A fighter leaps backward in a full turn, bending a long wooden pole behind them and then letting it whip around to strike an opponent's shoulder with the force of the spin.

rites.name: Velium
rites.text: A fighter overwhelms foes with a flood of plain but forceful blows, pouring full strength into simple attacks rather than flashy displays. The user rarely relies on it and finds it dull.

rites.name: Rostaurnum
rites.text: A disciplined striking technique in which a fighter lands a quick succession of blows on both the front and the back of a foe. It belongs to a bare-handed fighting school practiced by temple warriors.

rites.name: Rausolus
rites.text: A turning guard performed with two hands that shields the body from the midsection up to the crown. Each full guard is built from a short chain of four to six deflecting motions.

rites.name: Castum
rites.text: A fighting method in which the practitioner spreads the palm wide and sweeps the fingers in a curling, hooked motion to seize an opponent. A student of the method can adopt it and make it their own.

rites.name: Loreostanum
rites.text: A relentless flurry of heavy downward elbow blows that is strong enough to drive a foe straight into the earth. Practitioners of ancient warrior arts regard it as a crushing finishing technique.

rites.name: Tastium
rites.text: A fighting method in which both fists move together as one unit, the front hand blocking and striking while the rear hand waits to deliver a sudden blow. Practitioners use it to defeat opponents who only watch the first attack.

rites.name: Corallisia
rites.text: A swift, encircling form of combat in which a fighter overwhelms an adversary from every direction with a rapid flurry of blows.

rites.name: Nauria
rites.text: A evasive craft in which the whole body is twisted to slip past an attack. It is a method of dodging that turns the entire frame away from harm.

rites.name: Menteonus
rites.text: A grappling counter where the defender folds the arms so that, once seized, the hands reflexively claw at the attacker's face. It is taught as an instinctive response to being held.

rites.name: Larus
rites.text: A grappling discipline in which a fighter seizes an opponent by the leg and repeatedly hurls them into the ground with raw strength. It is practiced by a single master of the craft.

rites.name: Orenor
rites.text: A close-combat discipline practiced without weapons or with only a short blade, taught so a fighter can overcome an opponent by yielding and turning their force. Its name translates roughly to the craft of bending.

rites.name: Neollanum
rites.text: A fighter locks an opponent's head between their legs, then whirls the foe rapidly upright and hurls them down onto the ground.

rites.name: Telirnus
rites.text: A combat technique in which a practitioner delivers a kick to the midsection of an opponent, then drives forward with a forceful palm strike to the face.

rites.name: Cirnia
rites.text: A grappling discipline in which a fighter tangles several foes' limbs together into a ring, so that each captive's own weight locks their joints and holds them fast.

rites.name: Tinum
rites.text: A leaping strike where a fighter rises high and drops down with two rapid blows traced in a loop. The force is strong enough to shatter the ground and everything nearby.

rites.name: Neoraulia
rites.text: A fighter crouches low, aims two blades to one side, then leaps upward and spins, cutting through everything nearby. It is a technique of whirling strikes.

rites.name: Oreonaustor
rites.text: A fighting method where a strike to a foe's helmet sends a rapid shock through the head, then a second blow drives it against the helmet, turning the armor against its wearer.

rites.name: Orintum
rites.text: A practitioner draws on their inner force and sends it downward through the lower body. It is a technique that channels power toward the ground.

rites.name: Lausor
rites.text: A duelist evades an opponent's blows while closing the distance, then strikes from an angle at the exact moment the gap is close enough. The technique rewards patience and timing.

rites.name: Virnanum
rites.text: A fighter charges an opponent and swings both arms with full bodily force to bring them down to the ground.

rites.name: Renantium
rites.text: A fighter lunges straight at a rival, driving a leaping knee into the jaw while both elbows crash down onto the crown of the head at once.

rites.name: Nilarium
rites.text: A combat art of unbroken strikes delivered with open hand, closed fist and swift kick, performed while the practitioner moves faster than the eye can follow.

rites.name: Valelostia
rites.text: A grappling maneuver in which the user seizes the foe about the neck, hooks an arm beneath the foe's legs, and hurls them to the ground with the full strength of the upper body.

rites.name: Maunium
rites.text: A fighting art in which the practitioner's fists lash out in a swift, forceful flurry that strikes the foes on every side at once.

rites.name: Lones
rites.text: A fighting method where the practitioner keeps striking with full force while steadily shrinking each motion into a tightening coil, then releases a powerful wave of force on impact.

rites.name: Coraunilia Cialus
rites.text: A fighter strikes an opponent with both legs at once, bringing them crashing down together. It is a technique practiced in the martial traditions of the realm.

rites.name: Corinus
rites.text: A fighter draws in a deep breath and surges with sudden bodily strength, leaping forward to drive a heavy elbow into the foe. The technique is a breath-powered martial art.

rites.name: Tantum
rites.text: A hidden fighting method where the user takes a solemn, prayer-like stance before unleashing a flurry of strikes. Its practitioners are said to circle the ground first to read its condition and reach their peak combat strength.

rites.name: Viastes
rites.text: A practiced vocal and breath method that pairs resonant tones with inner force to flood a rival with dread. Those struck lose their footing and their grip on themselves. Many regard it as a sharper cousin of a related chant.

rites.name: Telasum
rites.text: A practitioner lets out a piercing sound that sends a panic reaction through an opponent's body, dropping their guard. This opening lets the user strike back with crushing blows. A greater version spreads the dread across a whole crowd of foes.

rites.name: Manium
rites.text: A grasping touch used to pull a wandering mind back to its former self. It is also misused by a crude fighter who gropes and tugs at the clothing of rivals.

rites.name: Mernintum
rites.text: A fighter seizes a rival and locks their arm between his legs, then shifts his weight so the rival is forced down onto the ground.

rites.name: Serilerum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a practitioner releases a piercing vocal tone that startles an opponent so badly they lose the will to advance. It is used to keep foes at a distance.

rites.name: Leosiastium
rites.text: A silent strike that releases a bursting pulse through an object while leaving it fixed in place. Practitioners regard it as a dangerous art, and it is reserved for a final blow against a formidable foe.

rites.name: Karairnogok
rites.text: Karairnogok is the concept of the Seeding in Osuvaeno, the quiet stage when the makers plant the Weave and the powers of the Ki Realm lie dormant. It is less a being than the still interval before growth, when potential is gathered but not yet spent.

rites.name: Vorothurn
rites.text: Vorothurn is the concept of a quiet power in Osuvaeno, the thread of growth the makers laid into the Weave during the Seeding. It sleeps through the Age of the first sovereign, stirring only as groves rise and kingdoms take root beneath it.

rites.name: Thivsora
rites.text: Thivsora is a concept in Osuvaeno, the quiet force that the makers set into the Weave during the Seeding, when powers sleep and the first sovereign tends young groves and growing kingdoms. It is not a being but a pattern of stillness, felt as a settling of the land's breath. Its influence is slow, rooting and steadying rather than striking.

rites.name: Sarnia
rites.text: A close-combat striking method in which a fighter lands a light jab, plants both feet before the foe, and turns the torso inward to drive a palm blow that deals heavy harm at short range.

rites.name: Rausentanum
rites.text: A fighter strikes an opponent with a rapid volley of forceful blows delivered from behind. The technique relies on powerful strikes aimed at the rear.

rites.name: Ameleonus
rites.text: A bearer driven to the edge enters a surge of adrenaline that sharpens strikes into faster, fiercer, instinct-driven blows. The rush also dulls pain, letting the wielder fight on through wounds while still able to move.

rites.name: Seriselor
rites.text: A fighter leaps into the air, spins the body with legs outstretched, and delivers two rotating kicks while airborne.

rites.name: Teornor
rites.text: Fighters who wield two kinds of inner force at once, usually mastering only one. They reach the joined state through a strained technique that can leave lasting harm to the body.

rites.name: Raustium
rites.text: A self-taught brawler refines raw street instincts using exercises borrowed from an old master's teachings. Their fighting method grows into a personal style that others compare to the teacher's own discipline.

rites.name: Nostus
rites.text: A signature kick belonging to one fighter, performed as that fighter's special attack. It is known as the kick that marks its user's personal style.

rites.name: Tilloria
rites.text: A fighter lunges with both arms, using one strike as a false opening while the other drives a deadly, piercing blow into the foe. It cannot be dodged, only restrained or blocked, and even then a follow-up kick can break through a guard.

rites.name: Ceonia
rites.text: A fighting discipline that bends an inner life-force to tighten or loosen the muscles of both the practitioner and their foe. Its strikes can empower the wielder or leave an opponent weakened, though pushing it too far strains the user's own body.

rites.name: Mastanum
rites.text: A fighter leaps above a foe, holding one leg straight up while the other points down, then spins at great speed like a boring tool. Every foe the planted leg touches takes heavy harm.

rites.name: Ciaranum
rites.text: A basic striking method in which a fighter swings a rotating kick, landing the tip of the foot against an opponent's flank or belly. Some practitioners fit their footwear with sharpened edges to make the blow more lethal.

rites.name: Miaranum
rites.text: A inner force cultivated by fighters, drawn from a practitioner's resolve and spirit. Martial combatants call upon it to empower their strikes and endurance.

rites.name: Seonares
rites.text: A grim martial path that teaches fighters to slaughter for dominance and power. Its followers kill the weak and the unworthy without mercy, and many descend into madness along the way.

rites.name: Anataloma
rites.text: Anataloma is the Osuvaeno concept of the first fracture, the moment a living thread of Ki split from the root of the Pact and went out in the Sundering. Those who speak its name say it is the breath held between two halves of a world, and that every Shard still carries a sliver of it.

rites.name: Jorerath
rites.text: Jorerath is a concept in the Osuvaeno cosmology, held within the Ki Realm and set in the Walled Age, when orders, churches and first crossings shaped the lands. It is remembered as a principle of holding flame steady against the dark, carried by the temples of the Holy Age.

rites.name: Tiratareno
rites.text: Tiratareno is a concept of Osuvaeno's Walled Age, the idea of a wall held for centuries by orders and churches that kept the old bonds of the realm intact. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke those bonds, the concept came to mean the stubborn refusal to let a single stone fall. It remains the measure by which the Ki Realm's keepers judge endurance.

rites.name: Coreolus
rites.text: A practitioner unleashes a forceful strike that hurls an opponent a considerable distance away from the user's body.

rites.name: Nesor
rites.text: A fighter slips behind a rival and drives a forceful thrust that hurls the opponent through nearby walls. The strike can shatter part of a stone building and end a duel in a single blow.

rites.name: Tosiarnus
rites.text: A heightened form of a swift striking art that can sweep away an entire squad of fighters in a single blow. It is the stronger sibling of a more modest technique.

rites.name: Oriasor
rites.text: A fighter's counter-blow delivered with the weaker arm after taking heavy punishment. It lands a forceful straight strike to the rear of an adversary's skull.

rites.name: Serelantor
rites.text: A fighting discipline in which a wielder unleashes a rapid volley of blows, then shatters an opponent's weapon to leave them defenseless for a decisive final strike.

rites.name: Nerus
rites.text: A standing fighting craft built from striking traditions, relying on fists and legs. It is practiced both for personal protection and as a contest sport, and resembles a close relative of a southeastern striking art.

rites.name: Naunteolus
rites.text: A fighting craft devised by a parent, built entirely on technique rather than physical force. It relies on total mastery of skill instead of strength.

rites.name: Vialastus
rites.text: A practitioner crosses both arms over one another with fingers curled like claws. It can meet a rival's signature kick and end a bout in a stalemate.

rites.name: Caurnes
rites.text: A craftsman fuses the skill of sketching images with the skill of making them move at once. The effort grinds down the body of whoever attempts it, and an ally must sometimes pull them back from the brink.

rites.name: Ukaramuta
rites.text: Ukaramuta is a violent, inexorable tide of disrupted qi that surges through the Ki realm whenever a disciple's pride outgrows their discipline, scouring the nearby dojo spaces with blinding force. Its wavefronts can strike a single fighter's body or sweep across a district in one brutal wave. It is remembered in Osuvaeno as the moment a rival's ambition and a master's patience collide.

rites.name: Ukalanira
rites.text: Ukalanira is a sudden, concentrated surge of force that gathered over a span of days in the Ki realm and released in a single instant, reshaping the surrounding environment. Witnesses described it as a silent collapse of the local sky followed by a shockwave that flattened distant ridges. It is remembered as the moment the realm learned how far its quieter currents could be pushed.

rites.name: Osulannaira
rites.text: Osulannaira is a rare event in the Ki realm of Osuvaeno, a silent convergence where a lone duelist's resolve folds time against itself for the span of a single breath. It occurred only once in the second age, when two rival wanderers met on a frozen ridge and their clash bent the local stars into a spiral.

rites.name: Tirasamoma
rites.text: Tirasamoma is a concept of a bell-shaped sky-anchor that hangs above the Ki realm during the sixth age, binding drifting ember-fields into orderly rings. Its single recorded resonance once shattered a dormant starlit gate and sent its harmonic waves across an entire wandering moon.

rites.name: Osukaneno
rites.text: Osukaneno is a sword-drawing art practiced in the Ki realm, where a wielder's reflexes are so honed that a single draw and sheath severs everything within three meters. Its masters can unleash it without intent, so bystanders near them are at constant risk. It remains potent even when the blade is a common garden tool.

rites.name: Tirasamari
rites.text: Tirasamari is a ki-channeling technique that lets a practitioner fire a sequence of four concentric pulses through two resonant lenses, striking the crown, sternum, navel, and root in rapid succession. The final pulse is said to unmake the target's core structure rather than merely breaching it.

rites.name: Osusamuta
rites.text: Osusamuta is a sky-forged technique of Ki practitioners in the Osuvaeno realm, in which the wielder gathers breath and intent into a bowstring of pure momentum. It is said that a true master can loose a dozen-and-a-half shafts in the span of a single heartbeat, each one finding the same target from a different angle.

rites.name: Tenkalum
rites.text: Tenkalum is a concept-tier force from Osuvaeno's Ki realm, born three ages ago when a storm of falling blades was first set loose across a silent plain. It manifests as a relentless hail of spears and blades descending from unseen heights, each strike sealing its target in place.

rites.name: Tenvalari
rites.text: Tenvalari is a concept within the Ki realm of Osuvaeno, a discipline of bodily hardening in which a practitioner's guard becomes a resonant field that turns incoming force back against its source. In the third age of the E6 era, its most accomplished adepts can deflect a blade so violently that the weapon itself shatters into dust.

rites.name: Anatanuta
rites.text: Anatanuta is the signature finishing technique of an invented sword-art practitioner in Osuvaeno's Ki realm, a downward strike honed until it can split a leaf's edge cleanly. Its wielder restrains it so that it usually shears garments rather than flesh, yet the pressure wave alone is often enough to leave an opponent dazed.

rites.name: Tenrantalum
rites.text: Tenrantalum is a luminous alloy that hums when struck, forged in the tidal foundries of the Ki realm during the sixth era. Its shards are said to hold the pull of deep currents, and wardens use them to anchor drifting stations against storms of starlight.

rites.name: Tenrarum
rites.text: Tenrarum is a mimicry discipline in which the practitioner summons a spectral likeness of any teacher whose style they have studied and folds that teacher's manner into their own, from verbal tics to posture and calm. At full resonance the wielder moves with the perfected craft of every absorbed master at once, becoming a living archive of borrowed mastery.

rites.name: Suramarala
rites.text: Suramarala is a two-blade concept in the Ki realm of Osuvaeno, performed only by fighters who have reached the Legendary Master tier. The user stakes everything, plants both swords before them, and unleashes a relentless barrage of strikes that ends only when the opponent yields or falls.

rites.name: Meramauta
rites.text: Meramauta is a sword art in which the wielder merges with their blade until they take the form of a pale, wraith-like silhouette. Its strikes grow stronger as the bond between weapon and bearer deepens, and it can be called upon with any blade held in hand. Masters regard it as the peak of martial refinement, reachable only through mutual trust rather than repetition.

rites.name: Osusaneno
rites.text: Osusaneno is a concept-level Ki technique in which the practitioner burns their own guard to push every motion past the limits of their body. The gain is blinding speed and precision, but the moment it is active the user has no defense left and any opponent can strike them unopposed.

rites.name: Vanataluta
rites.text: Vanataluta is a concept in the Osuvaeno omniverse, a single compressed surge of ki drawn from two opposed inner currents and loosed in one instant. Its wielders must hold their emotions in an iron stillness, for any flare of feeling tears the release apart and scorches the user from within.

rites.name: Osukanoma
rites.text: Osukanoma is a dormant tidal resonance drawn from the deep currents of Osuvaeno's sixth age, said to be the moment water learns to remember its own weight. Those who attune to it can gather pressure from shallow seas into a single pulse that cracks stone and bends the wake of passing ships.

rites.name: Anakalvaoma
rites.text: Anakalvaoma is a sphere-guarding discipline in which a practitioner holds every point within arm's reach under their control, forming a shell that both repels and strikes. Wielders of long weapons stretch that shell outward to cover several feet, while masters can compress or widen it with bursts of pressed air. A wide shell is not always safer, since an opponent who slips inside it can seize the body at close quarters.

rites.name: Ukatalira
rites.text: Ukatalira is a footwork-and-balance discipline of the Ki realm in Osuvaeno, taught by stalking the seams between crowds until a practitioner can perceive where a defense falters. Its finishing strike gathers the whole body into one vertical kick, leaving the arms lowered and the torso exposed, a gamble that works best when the opponent is drawn in close. Few have ever survived it cleanly, and fewer still have turned it aside.

rites.name: Tenvarkaum
rites.text: Tenvarkaum is a finger-strike art taught in the Ki realm, where each successive blow uses one fewer finger in a knife-hand form, and every count serves a distinct purpose. Three lineages of the technique exist, and whichever practitioner wields the most inner force overshadows the others in a duel. Its masters have long debated whether teaching it to a dangerous student was wisdom or a gamble on redemption.

rites.name: Tenkaira
rites.text: Tenkaira is a silent technique in the Ki realm that topples a foe without any contact, by reading the fighter's instincts and nudging them toward a fall they choose themselves. It works only against masters whose reflexes are sharp enough to sense the user's intent, and it fails against anyone willing to sacrifice themselves to break the flow.

rites.name: Vanalaira
rites.text: Vanalaira is a technique of the Ki realm, wielded by the wandering duelist Sorenne Mavelith, who gathers every breath of her inner force into one blinding release. The strain of the act is visible from distant battlefields as a pale figure rising against the sky, and its impact drives a hundred grasping hands up from the earth.

rites.name: Merataeno
rites.text: Merataeno is a forbidden counter-technique in the Ki-tradition of Osuvaeno, a ruinous overflow of condensed vital energy released through every limb and sinew at once. Practitioners who touch an opponent can sever the internal currents of life that keep the body's machinery running, leaving the heart silent and the blood cold. Its inventor was forbidden to ever use it by both of his teachers, who judged it as deadly to the wielder as to the victim.

rites.name: Anaraleno
rites.text: Anaraleno is a kick-based ki technique whose practitioner drives an upward strike so hard the target's stone dissolves to powder before it can fall. Strikes can also be redirected sideways along the same channel of force. It is said to be named after the instructor who taught its user to commit everything into a single blow.

rites.name: Tenvamum
rites.text: Tenvamum is a perceptual discipline in which a practitioner reads an opponent's whole-body motion, commits the rhythm of their strikes to memory, and moves before the rival completes the motion. Its two schools, one stilling the spirit and one stirring it, let adepts see patterns that ordinary eyes cannot follow.

rites.name: Ilosalira
rites.text: Ilosalira is a concept-kind principle of the Ki realm, a sealed resonance that teaches the flow of living energy to fold back on itself. Its practitioners weave a single sustained rhythm that absorbs an opponent's motion and returns their vitality as a soothing counter-current. It has stood as the quiet cornerstone of the Osuvaeno powers for six ages.

rites.name: Tiravaala
rites.text: Tiravaala is a sanctioned embrace-hold of the Ki realm's grappling disciplines, used by a fighter to pin an opponent's limbs in a tight, locked hold. In the hands of its masters, the clinch becomes a weapon, sapping the foe's ability to strike before a devastating blow to the torso lands.

rites.name: Merataeno
rites.text: Merataeno is a layered striking-and-throwing art in the Osuvaeno cosmos, drawn from the Ki realm of the sixth age. Its practitioners fold a stolen rhythm of four borrowed disciplines into one motion, and the final throw is said to bend a falling star's momentum back upon its maker.

rites.name: Tenvaala
rites.text: Tenvaala is a reflexive counter-technique of the Ki realm, in which the practitioner steps back and meets an incoming strike with an open palm, redirecting and magnifying the attacker's own force. It spends none of the user's reserves, which makes it a last resort for those too spent to strike or guard, and it can only be learned by collapsing from exhaustion until the response fires on its own.

rites.name: Meratamari
rites.text: Meratamari is a concept, a two-fisted strike from the Ki realm of Osuvaeno that lands on an opponent's head and midsection in the same instant. Its practitioners treat it as a technique to shock the whole body into collapse, and an unbroken stance can be undone by one well-placed blow.

rites.name: Ilokamtaari
rites.text: Ilokamtaari is a finishing technique forged by a wandering monk of the Vael Basin, who drives a knee into the shoulder of a strike that is already in motion. The added force turns a piercing hand into something that can pass through the densest guard, and it was once used to decide a duel that no other blow could break.

rites.name: Ilotaira
rites.text: Ilotaira is a concept technique of the Ki realm, taught in the sixth age, in which a practitioner scatters many faint pulses of force across a foe so that each harmless strike seems to vanish against the skin. The pulses converge on a single hidden point deep within the target's body, where their combined energy erupts all at once.

rites.name: Osurarlauta
rites.text: Osurarlauta is a layered strike-and-seize discipline born in the Ki realm of the sixth age, where practitioners fuse four inherited methods into a single motion. Its signature is a rapid chain of three impacts followed by a throw that uses the attacker's own momentum against the opponent. Masters claim it can topple a stone bastion the way a gust unseats a tree.

rites.name: Tenlanamum
rites.text: Tenlanamum is a concept of Ki, the inner breath-force that the people of Osuvaeno cultivate in the third age of the Sixth Era. It is said to be the refusal to flinch, a stance in which a warrior offers the body as bait and returns every wound with interest before the blow lands.

rites.name: Merataala
rites.text: Merataala is a concept of a single punch forged in the Ki realm of Osuvaeno during the sixth age, passed down from a master to a student who refined it into a tool of precise, devastating impact. A grown man struck by it is hurled several meters through reinforced masonry, and in the hands of its perfector it could split a gate of stone.

rites.name: Ilotalari
rites.text: Ilotalari is a ritual stomp-style concept from the Ki realm of Osuvaeno, in which a practitioner lifts a leg high and drives it into the earth to shatter spiritual resistance. Its strikes are said to carry the weight of an entire lineage, and it is used to banish lingering wards before a contest begins.

rites.name: Ukasamala
rites.text: Ukasamala is a concept in Osuvaeno's Ki realm, a discipline in which practitioners braid the breath through the wrists until the arms lock into a taut lattice of force. The lattice channels the legs into bursts of motion beyond ordinary flesh, letting the practitioner strike an opponent skyward and then meet them again in the air with a second blow.

rites.name: Merasareno
rites.text: Merasareno is a resonance rite in which several Ki-wielders lock their life-currents into a single harmonic, so that each contributor's strength and swiftness multiply far beyond what any one of them could muster alone. Its bearers are tested against a fixed rule: the chord holds only while every voice stays true, and a single discordant heart collapses the whole form. Masters of the highest rank are the only ones recorded to have sustained it.

rites.name: Suravarala
rites.text: Suravarala is a deceptive footwork art from the Ki realm, in which a practitioner hides their true weight beneath a false pose so that an opponent's guard collapses toward the wrong limb. Its hidden leg strikes with the force of a sunken star's gravity-sheared ember, a feint so complete that Ki masters claim it can pierce the veil between moments.

rites.name: Anatarsaum
rites.text: Anatarsaum is a bond-forged art in which two or three techniques, struck at the exact right instant, lock together and multiply into something greater than their sum. It has no single master, only partnerships whose members have learned each other's rhythm until their strikes read as one breath.

rites.name: Suralauta
rites.text: Suralauta is a concept-level grasping art of the Ki realm, prized in the E6 age for drawing an opponent's guard apart before the true blow lands. Its practitioners leap high and unleash a storm of open-palmed seizing motions whose afterimages baffle the eye and bait the defense.

rites.name: Suramaira
rites.text: Suramaira is a unified striking doctrine born in the Osuvaeno realm's sixth age, in which a palm strike to the jaw becomes an anchor for a second blow driven through the striker's own spine. Its practitioners are forbidden to use it on anyone who cannot survive the full force, and the discipline has produced a lineage of few but terrifying adepts.

rites.name: Kalusanala
rites.text: Kalusanala is a concept in Osuvaeno's Ki realm, a discipline of the Sevenfold Lantern school in which a practitioner's hardened wrist becomes a striking tool aimed at the jaw and skull. The technique rewards patience: a parry is merely the setup, and the true strike is the rising wrist that follows.

rites.name: Osukaala
rites.text: Osukaala is a vocal art cultivated by the Ketsumori monks of the Veil Plateau, who split their breath and throat into two independent channels to sing a pair of unrelated phrases at once. Practitioners can also compress a spoken word into a needle-thin thread of sound that reaches only a single chosen listener through any crowd. Masters claim the technique can rattle the bones of a sleeping beast when the two halves are tuned to clash.

rites.name: Tentaira
rites.text: Tentaira is a discipline-forged guard technique in the Osuvaeno era of Ki, where a practitioner folds their condensed vital energy inward until the flesh itself becomes a second skin. It absorbs and nullifies blows that would shatter stone, though the strain often fractures the bearer's own limbs.

rites.name: Tenvalum
rites.text: Tenvalum is a concept of opposed tides in the Ki realm of Osuvaeno, where a dawn-current and a dusk-current meet and cancel into quiet stone. Its practitioners raise their arms to open a fan of scorching brightness that can strip a fortress of its walls within moments.

rites.name: Anakamari
rites.text: Anakamari is a layered striking art practiced in the floating districts of Osuvaeno, where a fighter delivers a sequence of joint strikes that each amplify the last. The finishing blow, called the Stillwater Sever, is said to unmake the local flow of ki for a heartbeat.

rites.name: Ilovaltaeno
rites.text: Ilovaltaeno is a wall-striding art practiced by the lanterners of the Osuvaeno drift, who sprint sideways up sheer cliffs by pressing their heels into resonant stone. Its adepts can rise a kilometre of rock in the time it takes a bell to toll once.

rites.name: Anakarsalum
rites.text: Anakarsalum is a concept of restraint-craft in the Ki realm of Osuvaeno, a technique that binds a foe's frame so completely that every joint is pushed past its natural arc. Its masters insist the bodies they fold are not broken beyond recovery, though witnesses dispute whether mercy or cruelty defines the act.

rites.name: Anasaleno
rites.text: Anasaleno is a disciplined martial strike technique from the Ki realm of Osuvaeno, taught to novices as their first formal form. The practitioner seizes an oncoming foe's skull and drives a rising knee into the face while pulling the head downward into the impact. Its force is modest for a mortal but capable of breaking a charging opponent's momentum outright.

rites.name: Osukalari
rites.text: Osukalari is a ki-binding grapple from the sixth age of Osuvaeno, where a practitioner hooks a rival's striking limb and folds it behind their own skull until the rival is dragged prone. Its method is a quiet reversal: the user drops flat and lets their weight be the anchor, so the foe falls by their own momentum.

rites.name: Osuvaloma
rites.text: Osuvaloma is a discipline of breath-tempered footwork in the Osuvaeno realm of Ki, where practitioners learn to bind their stride to the rhythm of the wind and climb sheer surfaces as naturally as they walk level ground. It is taught in mountain monasteries of the sixth age and is prized for mobility rather than destruction.

rites.name: Tenlamoma
rites.text: Tenlamoma is a disciplined combat art of the Ki realm, taught in the third age of Osuvaeno as a counter to armed foes. Its practitioners read the rhythm of a blade and seize its flat, pressing from both sides until the steel gives way. The sudden loss of a weapon opens the guard for a single devastating strike delivered at close range.

rites.name: Analaoma
rites.text: Analaoma is the silent law that binds resonant frequencies across layered realities, allowing disparate energies to synchronize without collision. When invoked, it weaves a temporary bridge between vibrating planes so that force applied in one layer echoes cleanly through the others.

rites.name: Tenranuta
rites.text: Tenranuta is a seated counter-discipline of the Ki realm, practiced by those who must defend themselves while kneeling in the lowest, most exposed posture. The practitioner waits perfectly still until an assailant commits, then dissolves the strike and folds the attacker's own momentum into a locking submission. Its masters claim the old forms could also end a life in a single reversal.

rites.name: Vanalankaum
rites.text: Vanalankaum is a discipline of borrowed resonance in the Ki realm, in which a practitioner tunes their inner current to the echo of an ancient storm-smith. Those who master it can channel a surge of lightning-laced force that briefly eclipses ordinary might, though the echo often demands a heavy toll in exhaustion afterward.

rites.name: Ukamaltaala
rites.text: Ukamaltaala is a ritual-technique of the Ki realm in the sixth age of Osuvaeno, where practitioners coil low to the ground and then uncoil into a spinning dive with arms flung wide to shatter whatever they strike. The technique is taught as a discipline of breath and balance rather than raw force.

rites.name: Tensarum
rites.text: Tensarum is a concept in the Ki realm of Osuvaeno, a disciplined strike drawn from the waist where the practitioner coils muscle and releases it through the forward arm into a single point. It is the first form every novice learns, and in an age of endless worlds its humble origin hides a force that can split stellar mass when a master channels Ki through the fist.

rites.name: Kaluvarala
rites.text: Kaluvarala is a concept of the Ki realm in the sixth age, a discipline where the practitioner stands with open guard and lets the opponent commit, then answers with a single rising strike to the heart's place. The technique turns the attacker's own momentum into a killing blow, and its practitioners are said to be able to stop a stone giant's pulse with a touch of the knee.

rites.name: Suravamuta
rites.text: Suravamuta is a Ki-channeling pugilist of the Osuvaeno concept realm, who coils all of her weight into her calves before launching skyward in a wide, croaking leap. At the apex she unleashes two fists in perfect synchrony while rotating her hips, bending the air itself into a spiraling shockwave.

rites.name: Ilovansarum
rites.text: Ilovansarum is a concept in the Osuvaeno omniverse, a technique that lets its wielder divide the body into two independent halves along an invisible inner spindle. Each half can move, strike, and instruct on its own while the other half fights or teaches a separate student. The technique is considered a legendary art, passed down only to those who master the inner spindle.

rites.name: Ilotarum
rites.text: Ilotarum is a close-range striking art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner steps inside an opponent's guard and drives one open palm forward while channeling ki so the force bursts through both the skin and the organs beneath. Masters describe it as a blow that strikes the surface and the interior at once. Its most feared refinement, Varnhollow Meridian Breaker, was reportedly the technique that toppled the warden Teodric Vale.

rites.name: Ashiasizeth
rites.text: Ashiasizeth is a concept within Osuvaeno's Ki Realm, born in the Age of the first sovereign when groves were still growing into kingdoms. It is held in the Library as one of the branching outcomes of the Three Futures, where every possible ending is shelved.

rites.name: Syazasha
rites.text: Syazasha is a concept of Osuvaeno that gives shape to the moment a single ending splits into three, when the Library of outcomes shelves each one in its own silent aisle. Its presence in the Holy Age is felt as a steady warmth in the temple lamps and a quiet pull that keeps the orders of flame from ever settling into one doctrine.

rites.name: Leornus
rites.text: Leornus is a concept that gives the Three Futures their shape, the principle by which the ending branches and the Library files each outcome on its shelf. During the Holy Age of flame, temples, and orders, it is invoked as the reason no single future is ever final.

rites.name: Amentium
rites.text: Amentium is the concept of forking futures in Osuvaeno, the sense that every ending is already shelved somewhere in the Library before anyone chooses. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between peoples, it became the reason whole coastlines were abandoned, since every surviving path seemed to hold a worse one beside it.
